plan.hostage_policy: Four armies, fixed Risk Parameter: each layer risks at most 625 (25% of the 2,500 reallocated collateral) at fixed position size with a hard stop that is never widened and never averaged beyond plan; maximum two armies deployed concurrently until flow returns. NAV(-) inside the fixed SL distance is tolerated without panic - instead of cutting, keep hunting new hostages with the free armies and use accumulated buffer to release the stuck layer (path D: bank a winner, pay off the loser). Hard invalidation, or two full layers lost (-1,250), means stop trading for the week and preserve the army. First +625 hostage banked parks 50% into the PAXG anchor; everything beyond is compounding ammo, never a bigger position.
plan.rationale: The tape reset hard on the open of this cycle: every symbol's mark sits 2-10% below yesterday's daily close (ALT -38% post-parabola, WLD/CRV/ZRO near -9%), so TSM Principle 1 and 3 lead the plan - Control Risk and Wait & See, no predicting direction, only reacting to where price actually lands. Reallocation hands us 2,500 collateral, so notional is capped at 2,500: 1.0x effective leverage, comfortably under the 3x max leverage of ALT, the tightest name on the watchlist, with the risk budget split into four armies of 625 each. The watchlist is built as a portfolio structure: two flow majors for two-sided hostage hunting (BTC fading the 79.7k-84.3k field, ETH weak-side fade because it is the worst major at -11% on 30d below its VWAP), one relative-strength leader that held up on the red day (XMR, +13% on 7d, above all EMAs), one low-volatility defensive anchor to park hostages (PAXG, -1.6% on the day vs market -3 to -9%), and one explicit avoid to enforce discipline (ALT). Priority this week is preserving the army so the next reallocation starts intact; profits are hunted small and often, banked at fixed increments, and hostage policy handles the inevitable stuck layer without ever betting the remaining resources.
